title: Morgan and Santa Claus the Impossible and the External-Finite System
tale:
Once upon a time, there was once an old barn that stood in the middle of a deep gloomy New Haven, and in the barn lived Morgan.

Morgan lived with Elfin Payton, Agile Chloe, Lennon the Childish, Blunt Alexandra, Rowan the Churlish, and Brienne of Tarth the Powerful.

Smart Rachel, Hateful Finley, Reluctant Megan, Joan of Arc the Agile, and Maria the Persevering were known to Morgan.

A selfish person known as Jordan came into the region of New Haven.

Jordan the Unpleasant issued an order to kill. It required proof. THIS WAS CRUEL.

Morgan bumped into Kind David.

"Well, look who this is, it's David" rumbled Morgan the Apprehensive.

"Welcome, Morgan the Apprehensive" retorted David.

"Well, you certainly are numb," remarked Morgan the Apprehensive.

"Yes, I am," conceded David. "But it's been said that I'm also kind!"

"Here," said David, "you'll need this," and gave Morgan the Apprehensive the Multi-phase Rift.

"What's this?" asked Morgan.

"What does it look like?" replied David. "It's a special, magical Multi-phase Rift. Perhaps you can use it in your struggle with Jordan the Unpleasant."

"I have a tale for you," said Kind David, "Morgan the Apprehensive of Nizhny Novgorod Oblast:"



Jordan the Unpleasant throws Morgan into the well.

Too bad Morgan had a considerable attachment to breathing.

When G-d calls one home, there is never room for argument. There is much wailing in New Haven.



"And now," concluded Kind David, "my tale is done."

Morgan was a bit taken aback by the tale.

"Oh, it's you, Jordan the Unpleasant" exclaimed Morgan the Apprehensive.

"Oh, it's you, Morgan the Apprehensive" replied Jordan the Unpleasant.

"Well, you certainly are selfish," rumbled Morgan the Apprehensive.

"Yes, I am," conceded Jordan the Unpleasant. "But it's been said that I'm also unpleasant!"

"Don't go bragging like that!" says Morgan the Apprehensive

Jordan the Unpleasant arrives and thrusted his arm in at the window. Morgan the Apprehensive cut off the bony thing, and Jordan the Unpleasant disappeared, howling, leaving his arm behind.

Such behavior could not be tolerated: Morgan the Apprehensive fell upon Jordan, bound him with ropes. Jordan the Unpleasant was completely burnt to cinders. And Jordan the Unpleasant sits to this day in the pit - in Tartarus.

One evening, there came into the region of New Haven a very smart person known as Andrew.

A false substitution was perpetrated by Andrew.

Morgan encountered Kind David again.

"Here," said Kind David, "you'll need this," and gave Morgan the Apprehensive the Linear-External-Linear-Electron Generator.

"What's this?" asked Morgan.

"What does it look like?" replied Kind David. "It's a special, magical Linear-External-Linear-Electron Generator. Perhaps you can use it in your struggle with Andrew the Crabby."

"I have a tale for you," said David, "Morgan the Apprehensive and the dismissal of Andrew and Hayden the Banal:"



Morgan went down to the a small stream, stripped off her clothes, and went into the water. Then there came a man out of the water and sat on top of Morgan the Apprehensive's clothes. She tried to drive the man away, but he stuck and would not move.

Morgan the Apprehensive pops to the top of the water like a cork.

So Morgan hung, drawn, and quartered Andrew. Afterwards Morgan the Apprehensive heaps up a pile of wood, sets fire to it, burnts Andrew on the pyre, and scatters his ashes to the wind. But Andrew sits to this day in the pit - in Tartarus.

Morgan went down to the a local lake, stripped off her clothes, and went into the water. Then there came a griffin out of the water and sat on top of Morgan the Apprehensive's clothes. She tried to drive the griffin away, but she stuck and would not move.

Morgan pops to the top of the water like a cork.

Morgan the Apprehensive greeted the banal griffin, and caught hold of her right little finger. Hayden the Banal tried to shake she off, flying first about the house and then out of it, but all in vain. At last the banal griffin after soaring on high, struck the ground, and fell to pieces, becoming a fine yellow sand. And that is that. And the banal griffin sits to this day in the pit - in Tartarus.

Morgan was such an awful drunkard as passes all description. Well, one day she went to a kabak, intoxicated herself with liquor, and then went staggering home blind drunk. Now her way happened to lie across a river. When she came to the river, she didn't stop long to consider, but kicked off her boots, hung them round her neck, and walked into the water. Scarcely had she got half-way across when she tripped over a stone, tumbled into the water - and there was an end of her.

When G-d calls one home, there is never room for argument. There is much wailing in New Haven.



"And now," concluded David, "my tale is done."

Morgan the Apprehensive was a bit taken aback by the tale.

"Greetings, Andrew" mused Morgan.

"Hail and well met, Morgan" returned Andrew.

"Well, you certainly are smart," muttered Morgan.

"Yes, I am," conceded Andrew. "But it's been said that I'm also crabby!"

Morgan the Apprehensive and Andrew engaged in battle.

So Morgan the Apprehensive cut the feet off from Andrew the Crabby and placed him on a stump by the roadside. So they placed him in a coffin, and carried it to church, whereupon it burst into horrible flames, singeing the hands of those who dared carry it.

When nobody was paying attention in New Haven, a confident bat known as Maternal DEATH strode in.

Maternal DEATH caused bodily injury, maiming, mutilation. Oh!

Morgan encountered David again.

"Here," said Kind David, "you'll need this," and gave Morgan the Apprehensive the External-Phase-Internal Rupture.

"What's this?" asked Morgan the Apprehensive.

"What does it look like?" replied David. "It's a special, magical External-Phase-Internal Rupture. Perhaps you can use it in your struggle with DEATH."

"I have a tale for you," said Kind David, "Morgan the Apprehensive and what she did in Nizhny Novgorod Oblast:"



Bat siezed Morgan, placed her in a barrel, and flung the barrel into the murky pond.

Too bad Morgan had a considerable attachment to breathing.

When G-d calls one home, there is never room for argument. There is much wailing in New Haven.



"And now," concluded David, "my tale is done."

Morgan the Apprehensive was a bit taken aback by the tale.

"Hail and well met, Maternal DEATH" mused Morgan the Apprehensive.

"Welcome, Morgan the Apprehensive" muttered Maternal DEATH.

"Well, you certainly are maternal," remarked Morgan the Apprehensive.

"Yes, I am," conceded Maternal DEATH. "But it's been said that I'm also confident!"

DEATH turned into a bat, and Morgan bridled her, led her into the yard, and jumped on her back. The bat carried her off over hills and dales and ravines, and did all she could to try and throw her rider. But no! Morgan the Apprehensive stuck on tight, and thumped her over the head like anything with the aspen cudgel, and went on treating her with a taste of the cudgel until she knocked her off her feet, and then pitched into her as she lay on the ground, gave her another half-dozen blows or so, and at last beat DEATH to death.

So Morgan cut the feet off from the confident bat and placed her on a stump by the roadside. The confident bat was completely burnt to cinders. And Maternal DEATH sits to this day in the pit - in Tartarus.

There came into the region of New Haven a enterprising individual known as Emerson the Fabulous.

Morgan's bride was forgotten after Emerson the Fabulous cast a spell.

Morgan met David again.

"Here," said Kind David, "you'll need this," and gave Morgan the Auxiliary-Linear-Neural-Linear Singularity.

"What's this?" asked Morgan the Apprehensive.

"What does it look like?" replied Kind David. "It's a special, magical Auxiliary-Linear-Neural-Linear Singularity. Perhaps you can use it in your struggle with Emerson."

"Thanks!" said a thankful Morgan the Apprehensive thankfully.

"I have a tale for you," said Kind David, "The account of Morgan the Apprehensive and Emerson:"



In a certain barn lived Morgan the Apprehensive.

Morgan lives with Elfin Payton, Agile Chloe, Lennon the Childish, Blunt Alexandra, Rowan the Churlish, and Brienne of Tarth the Powerful.

Smart Rachel, Hateful Finley, Reluctant Megan, Joan of Arc the Agile, and Maria the Persevering are known to Morgan.

New Haven plays host to a enterprising person, Emerson.

Emerson attemptes to deceive victim.

Morgan the Apprehensive unwittingly helps Emerson the Fabulous.

Hungry and faint, Morgan wandered on, walked farther and farther and at last came to where stood the house of Emerson. Round the house were set twelve poles in a circle, and on each of eleven of these poles was stuck a human head, the twelfth alone remained unoccupied.

Elfin Payton, a friend of Morgan the Apprehensive, needs money or means of existence. Times are tough.

"Hello, Emerson" remarks Morgan.

"Hail and well met, Morgan" mutters Emerson.

"Well, you certainly are fabulous," rumbles Morgan.

"Yes, I am," concedes Emerson. "But it's been said that I'm also enterprising!"

In the evening Morgan went to the church. Twelve o'clock struck, the coffin lid fell to the ground, Emerson the Fabulous jumped up and began tearing from side to side, and threatening her. Then he conjured up horrors, this time worse than before. It seemed to her as if a fire had broken out in the church; all the walls were wrapped in flames! But she held her ground and went on reading, never once looking behind herself. Just before daybreak Emerson rushed to his coffin - then the fire seemed to go out immediately, and all the deviltry vanished!

And Emerson is given a tongue-lashing by Morgan. Thanks to Morgan the Apprehensive, Emerson the Fabulous was completely burnt to cinders. Emerson sits to this day in the pit - in Tartarus.

Morgan the Apprehensive set out for her barn.

So she went and had a goodish drink, and then started in search of New Haven.



"And now," concluded David, "my tale is done."

"Hello there, Emerson the Fabulous" noted Morgan the Apprehensive.

"Salutations! Morgan the Apprehensive" volleyed Emerson the Fabulous.

"Well, you certainly are fabulous," said Morgan the Apprehensive.

"Yes, I am," conceded Emerson the Fabulous. "But it's been said that I'm also enterprising!"

Morgan and Emerson the Fabulous engaged in battle.

Seeing that Emerson the Fabulous was perfectly enfeebled, Morgan the Apprehensive snatched up her Auxiliary-Linear-Neural-Linear Singularity, and with a single blow struck off Emerson's head. Behind her voices began to cry: "Strike again! Strike again! Or he will come to life!" "No," replied Morgan, "a hero's hand does not strike twice, but finishes its work with a single blow." The body was left in the possession of Morgan the Apprehensive, who scraped together the pieces and burned them in the stove.

New Haven played host to a appalling individual, Santa Claus the Impossible after breakfast.

Santa Claus declared war on Morgan the Apprehensive.

Morgan came across David again.

"Here," said Kind David, "you'll need this," and gave Morgan the Apprehensive the External-Finite System.

"What's this?" asked Morgan the Apprehensive.

"What does it look like?" replied Kind David. "It's a special, magical External-Finite System. Perhaps you can use it in your struggle with Santa Claus."

"Thanks!" said a thankful Morgan.

"I have a tale for you," said Kind David, "Morgan the Apprehensive and Santa Claus the Impossible and the External-Finite System:"



Man siezed Morgan, placed her in a barrel, and flung the barrel into a local lake.

Morgan had never learned to swim.

These things happen. Unfortunately. There is much wailing in New Haven.



"And now," concluded Kind David, "my tale is done."

Morgan the Apprehensive was a bit taken aback by the tale.

"Well, look who this is: Santa Claus" mused Morgan the Apprehensive.

"Oh, hello, Morgan the Apprehensive" replied Santa Claus.

"Well, you certainly are impossible," remarked Morgan the Apprehensive.

"Yes, I am," conceded Santa Claus. "But it's been said that I'm also appalling!"

And they set to work fighting; the dust flew like anything. They'd have gone on fighting ever so much longer, only the cocks began to crow.

And Santa Claus the Impossible was hung, drawn, and quartered by Morgan the Apprehensive. And they placed him in a coffin, and carried it to church, whereupon it burst into horrible flames, singeing the hands of those who dared carry it.

Morgan settled down and dated for a few years, but decided to remain single. After that she lived long and happily, survived to a great age, and then died peacefully.

All of this took place long before you were born, so it's not surprising that you don't remember it. But it happened, and people speak of it still.
